Sam H.: Hey team — quick design review for an inline credentials row that surfaces a lightweight lifecycle (create -> rotate -> revoke) without jumping to modals. Figma: https://figma.com/s/inline-cred-row-mock Anya P.: Curious about benefits? fewer clicks and faster rotate workflows? Sam H.: Exactly. The idea: row expands in-place to show a compact timeline, last-used info, and primary actions (rotate, disable, copy id). A 'Manage details' link opens the full drawer for scopes/IPs/KMS. Lee R.: Love fewer context switches. Concern: advanced settings discoverability (scopes, IP allowlist). Are we hiding critical security controls too deep? Sam H.: Not hiding — primary actions inline, but any change to scopes or key lifespan opens the detailed drawer. Inline is for quick ops only. Morgan (design): Copy tweaks: inside the inline view use "Disable" for the quick revoke action — feels less final. Reserve "Revoke permanently" with a strong warning inside the manage drawer. Add an obvious inline badge for admin-scoped keys: small red-outlined "Admin". Ida (a11y): A11y items: when expanding, move focus into the expansion and announce "Key details expanded for " via aria-live. When revealing a secret, ensure screen readers don't persist it in the accessibility tree after it's hidden. Sam H.: Proposed aria snippet:
Key details expanded for MyService-Prod
Sam H.: Rotate flow: inline rotate starts a soft-rotate with a 30-minute overlap where both old/new tokens are valid. We display a countdown and an "Undo rotate" primary inline CTA during overlap. Lee R.: Countdown needs accessible color contrast. Keyboard users need an easy Undo — make it a visible primary button while available. Anya P.: Create flow — still a modal, but we reduce friction: prefill name from service, default scope to "read-only", and strong microcopy: "Secret shown once — download now or copy to a secure vault." Primary CTA: "Download secret"; secondary: "Show & copy". Morgan (design): Empty-state copy suggestion: "No API keys yet. Create one to integrate Redwood into your app. Start with a dev key (read-only) and rotate before production." Offer a tiny quick-start snippet that can be copied. Ida (a11y): For empty state, auto-focus the "Create key" CTA and add aria-describedby pointing to hidden guidance: "Start with read-only keys for testing." Make the quick-start code block tabbable and give it role="region". Sam H.: Edge case: revoking a key that has active clients. Proposed confirm copy: "This will immediately stop any clients using this key. Consider rotating instead to avoid downtime. Revoke anyway?" Anya P.: Shorter phrasing suggestion: "This will immediately stop clients using this key." Cleaner. Lee R.: Add telemetry in the expansion: last used timestamp, top IPs (masked), and a tiny sparkline of recent usage to help decide if revoke is safe. Sam H.: Implementation note: only show last 10 IPs and mask them for privacy. deploy-bot: deploy:deploy-preview #api-keys-inline successful — preview: https://preview.redwood.ai/keys-inline Morgan (design): Copy-to-clipboard toast should be transient and use role="status" with message "Secret copied to clipboard" so SRs announce it once. Ida (a11y): Mask toggle should use aria-pressed and update label text between "Show secret" and "Hide secret". Lee R.: Visual nits: use an amber safety token for inline "Disable" instead of full red used for permanent revoke. Ensure contrast ratios pass. Ida (a11y): Focus order inside expanded row: key name -> last used -> primary action -> manage details. Sam H.: I'll update mocks with these changes and push prototype to dev next week for keyboard/a11y review. If no objections I'll proceed. :thumbsup: Anya P.: 👍 Lee R.: Thanks, looks good. Morgan (design): small follow-up: can we show a subtle banner in the console when a key is within the rotate overlap window? helps reduce mistakes. Sam H.: Good idea, will mock a slim banner above the row. I'll post updated link by EOD Friday.
